summary: Decimal constructed from a string preserves its decimal digits without first converting through binary floating point.
documentation: Decimal constructed from a string preserves its decimal digits without first converting through binary floating point. quantize rounds to a chosen exponent; an explicit ROUND_HALF_UP rule resolves exact halfway cases away from zero.
inputs: A list of finite decimal strings with small magnitudes and at most six fractional digits.
caution: Use the application’s agreed rounding policy rather than assuming all systems share this rule. Constructing Decimal from a float carries the float’s approximation. Decimal can preserve a negative zero sign.
scenarios: Format an imported decimal amount under an explicitly agreed rounding rule.
Compare exact halfway cases in a billing preview.
Generate reproducible decimal fixtures without binary-float conversion.
title: Round decimal text explicitly
problem: Convert each decimal string directly to Decimal, quantize to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP, and return fixed-point strings with exactly two decimal places. Preserve a negative-zero sign if rounding produces one.
hint: Import Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP; format each quantized result with f.
goal: Use Decimal.quantize() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
